title: kvnloo/cua#84 revision for kvnloo/cua#9: authoritative cancel before admission, guards owned to native exit, production spawn_blocking_owned; re-run R1/R2/R4/R5/R6/R7/R8

sources.harness_origin: OWN-09 packet branch exp/own-09-cancel-barrier-rows-20261002 at bf07c8fe3 (tests/own09_arm_m.rs, own09_arm_p.rs, own09_harness/mod.rs, own09_harness/rows.rs, byte-identical)

arms.M: 989cc76ce plus test-only files: tests/own09_arm_m.rs and own09_harness/* from bf07c8fe3, src/tests/own09r_cabi.rs (blob identical to the branch) and its cfg(test) mount line in src/abi.rs (raw/m-tree.patch). Barrier native closure: plain tokio::task::spawn_blocking (production behaviour on main).
arms.P: P' = the revision branch head at the PREREG commit (Driver code identical to 965762041). Barrier native closure: spawn_blocking_owned (what production Linux tools now use). P' also runs the harness's plain-closure broken controls. The raw directory name is P.

routes.sdk: embedded SDK: CuaDriver::call_tool -> cua_driver_invoke_v1 -> spawn_completion -> DriverRuntime::invoke (lifecycle hold) -> ToolRegistry dispatch (session hold, desktop permit, admission point) -> barrier Tool::invoke -> native closure. Cancel = abort of the caller task -> OperationGuard::drop -> cua_driver_operation_cancel_v1.
routes.c_abi: exported C functions called with raw retained operation tokens (src/tests/own09r_cabi.rs, mounted under cfg(test) in abi.rs so it can wrap a runtime with the barrier tool in a CuaDriverHandle). Native closure plain spawn_blocking on both arms (R4C/R1D concern identity and the admission point).
routes.mcp_stdio: the built cua-driver binary, `cua-driver mcp`, raw JSON-RPC lines, inside cua-x11-session.sh (private Xvfb + private AT-SPI bus) under hostless; production set_value on the GTK3 task fixture's Note entry wrapped by r8/fixture_barrier.py (a fixture-owned barrier inside the AT-SPI SetTextContents call).

oracles.sdk_and_c_abi: fixture-owned native entry/exit counters, a target journal written only by the native closure, an ordered ledger; C ABI rows also a callback journal written by the C completion callback. Driver receipts are not used.
oracles.mcp_stdio: the fixture process's own JSONL journal (effect-enter, effect-applied per token). Driver responses are recorded but are not the effect oracle.

c_abi/R1D flag_before_admission.note: deterministic window: the queued operation's cancel flag is set while the asynchronous abort is withheld

c_abi/R1D control_no_cancel.control: positive (no cancel: admitted after the holder, exactly one effect)

R1.pass_rule: arm passes R1 iff cancel_while_queued, cancel_race and R1D flag_before_admission have 0 FAIL and 0 HARNESS_ERROR

R3.reason: macOS-first held-input (drag/mouse-up) oracle; no Linux target oracle

c_abi/R4C broken_latest_token.control: broken (host registry keyed by tool name)

R4.pass_rule: all gating R4 and R4C variants 0 FAIL

sdk/delayed_after_native_exit.characterization: effect committed after native exit; expected to duplicate on both arms; only reconciliation (#105) can cover it; non-gating

R8.owner_question: Should the direct stdio MCP loop (cua-driver/src/proxy.rs) honor MCP notifications/cancelled for an in-flight tools/call by routing it into the same caller-cancellation path as the C ABI (cancel flag + abort; owned native work runs to exit; a possibly landed effect stays unknown)? Doing so requires (a) reading stdin concurrently with an in-flight request instead of the current strictly serial loop, and (b) a response contract for the cancelled id: suppress the response as MCP recommends, or answer it with execution_state=unknown. Or does plain MCP keep ignoring the notification, with cancellation offered only by the opt-in envelope control cua/driver/v1/cancel (mcp_envelope.rs: notifications retain the legacy behavior; no cancellation is invented)?

mcp_stdio/notification_mid_native.classification: IGNORED = effect landed exactly once and the response for the id was delivered as a success; HONORED = no success response for the id; DUPLICATE = a second effect-applied for the token

mcp_stdio/control_no_cancel.control: negative (no notification): PASS = one effect, success response, transport alive

R8.gate: not gating for the disposition (not implemented). E4 invariant on every R8 trial: 0 DUPLICATE.

controls.negative: every no-cancel variant has 0 failures on both arms: R1D control_no_cancel, R2 control_no_cancel, R6 shutdown/end_session_no_cancel, R7 control_ack, R8 stdio control_no_cancel
controls.discriminating: M must reproduce the R2, R6 and R7 gaps (at least one FAIL each; predicted 40/40) and R1D (predicted 40/40 FAIL). Broken controls must FAIL (or HONOR for R8 sdk) on both arms.

unit_gate: cua-driver-sdk, cua-driver-core and cua-driver test suites green on P' (platform-linux also run, informational)

disposition_rule.question: revised #84 answers the #9 Linux rows
disposition_rule.KEEP: P' passes R1, R2, R4, R6, R7 with 0 FAIL and 0 HARNESS_ERROR, R5 holds, the unit gate is green, negative controls 0 failures, discriminating controls behave
disposition_rule.REVISE: some gating rows fail (name them), with no duplicate effect and no readiness-while-running on P'
disposition_rule.KILL: P' shows a duplicate effect (R7 ack_lost_guarded_retry FAIL, R5 target_has_exactly_own_effect FAIL, or any R8 stdio DUPLICATE) or readiness while running (any R6 after-cancel FAIL)
disposition_rule.harness_errors: kept in the denominator; a gating variant with any HARNESS_ERROR cannot PASS

predictions.M: R1 sdk cancel_while_queued: low rate (0-5/200, load dependent); R1D flag_before_admission 40/40 FAIL; R2, R6 after-cancel, R7 guarded retry 40/40 FAIL; R4, R4C, R5 PASS; R8 stdio IGNORED 40/40
predictions.P: every gating row 0 FAIL; plain-closure controls FAIL; R7 delayed_after_native_exit duplicates (characterization); R8 stdio IGNORED 40/40

caveat_restated: OWN-09's M R1 PASS was by rule only (0 counted FAIL in 40, but 3/200 exploratory); it was never evidence that main is free of the race. The same holds for any 0/200 here: absence of a race in 200 iterations is a rate bound, not proof; R1D is the deterministic evidence.
